English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
dada (disambiguation)
Wikipedia

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio (US):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

Imitative of a child's first syllables; see dad.

Noun

[edit]

dada (plural dadas)

  1. (childish) Father, dad.

Etymology 2

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

dada (uncountable)

  1. Alternative letter-case form of Dada (“cultural movement”).

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Adad, adda, daad

Crimean Tatar

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Ottoman Turkish دادا (dâdâ, “nanny, nurse”), from Persian دادا (dâdâ, “nanny, nurse”). Compare Turkish dadı and Serbo-Croatian dàdilja.

Noun

[edit]

dada

  1. (Northern) older sister
    Synonyms: apte, abla, tata

Declension

[edit]

ablative dadadan

Dutch

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈdaː.daː/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: da‧da

Etymology 1

[edit]

From French dada (literally “hobby horse”).

Noun

[edit]

dada n (uncountable, no diminutive)

  1. dada, the cultural movement
    Synonym: dadaïsme

Adjective

[edit]

dada (invariable, comparative meer dada, superlative meest dada)

  1. related to the dada art movement
  2. bizarre, irrational, like dada art

Etymology 2

[edit]

Interjection

[edit]

dada

  1. (childish) bye-bye
    Zeg dada aan oma. ― Say bye-bye to granny.

Adverb

[edit]

dada

  1. (childish) away
    Oma gaat dada. ― Granny is going away now.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • daad

dada
Wikipedia id

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Malay dada, from Proto-Malayic *dada, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *dahdah, from Proto-Austronesian *daSdaS.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈdada/ [ˈda.da]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ada
  • Syllabification: da‧da

Noun

[edit]

dada (plural dada)

  1. (anatomy) chest, thorax
  2. (anatomy) chest cavity, thoracic cavity
    Synonyms: rongga dada, ruang dada

Irish

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • dadadh, dadaí, dadaidh, dadamh
  • tada (Cois Fharraige)

Etymology

[edit]

Modification of adamh (“atom”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈd̪ˠad̪ˠə/

Pronoun

[edit]

dada

  1. iota, jot, whit, tittle
  2. (chiefly in the negative) anything, nothing
    Níl dada ann. ― There's nothing there.
    Ní fheicim dada. ― I can't see anything.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • dada beo

Malay

[edit]
Malay Wikipedia has an article on:
dada
Wikipedia ms

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Malayic *dada, from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *dahdah, from Proto-Austronesian *daSdaS.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (schwa-variety) IPA(key): /ˈdadə/ [ˈda.də]
    • Rhymes: -adə, -də, -ə
  • (Baku) IPA(key): /ˈdada/ [ˈda.da]
    • Rhymes: -ada, -da, -a
  • Hyphenation: da‧da

Noun

[edit]

dada (Jawi spelling دادا, plural dada-dada or dada2)

  1. (anatomy) chest, breast
  2. (figurative) seat of emotions: heart
    Synonym: hati

Verb

[edit]

dada (active mendada, third-person passive didada)

  1. Bare form of mendada (“to confront or face something or someone”).

  • berdada-dadaan
  • dadaan
  • mendada
Compounds

  • tulang dada
